problem:
Which of the following is a $4\times 3$ matrix?

$$
L=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}],\,M=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 5 & \sqrt{2} & 7\end{aligned}],\,N=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 \\ 3 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

examples.knowledge_point: Identifying a Matrix by Its Description
examples.problem:
Which of the following is a $3 \times 2$ matrix?

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -5 \\ 0 & 1.1 & \sqrt{2}\end{aligned}]
$$
examples.worked_solution:
- The matrix $A$ has $2$ rows and $3$ columns. So, its dimensions are $2 \times 3.$ $\quad{\color{red}\times}$

- The matrix $B$ has $3$ rows and $2$ columns. So, its dimensions are $3 \times 2.$ $\quad{\color{green}\checkmark}$

- The matrix $C$ has $1$ rows and $3$ columns. So, its dimensions are $1 \times 3.$ $\quad{\color{red}\times}$

Therefore, only $B$ is a $3 \times 2$ matrix.

feedback.problem: What are the dimensions of the matrix $K$, where $K=[\begin{aligned}0\end{aligned}]?$
feedback.worked_solution: The matrix $K$ has $1$ row  and $1$ column.  So,  its dimensions are  $1\times 1.$
